Stormwater Utility System The stormwater system serves nearly 7,700 parcels. Due to minimal projected customer growth, baseline revenues are expected to stay flat at around $1.4 million annually through the forecast period. The FY 2026 budget relies on existing cash reserves to balance. While effective short-term, a long- term rate adjustment is required to avoid completely depleting these funds. Operating expenses have risen nearly 8% per year since 2021. The 2026 budget sits at $1.3 million and is projected to scale 3.8% annually to $1.6 million by 2031, driven by inflation, labor (4%), and health insurance (10%). The total stormwater capital improvement plan is $140.9 million (2026– 2031). $132.8 million will be covered externally via the Resiliency Fund. $8.1 million must be absorbed by the stormwater fund itself ($3.4 million via user rates and $4.8 million via new debt). The system is paying $256,000 annually on a 2015 revenue note, which will be paid off in 2030. To help fund the capital plan, a new State Revolving Fund (SRF) loan of roughly $353,000 annually will come online in 2030, seamlessly replacing the old debt.

Reserves will be strategically drawn down over the first three years to cushion the blow to consumers while still tracking toward the 90- day rate revenue reserve target by 2031. The recommended rate path was for 1 5% annual increases for 2027, 2028, and 2029, followed by smaller 6.5% increases in 2030 and 2031. This results in a cumulative rate adjustment of 72.5%. The initial 2027 rate places the city slightly above the regional surveyed average of $158.48 per year. Unlike the reclaimed water system, an alternative "smoothed" capital reduction plan cannot be calculated here. Because stormwater is billed as an assess ment, legally, the base fee can only fund city-wide improvements. The $132.8 million in resilience projects provide localized benefits to specific areas. If the city wishes to fund those projects outside the Resiliency Fund, it would legally have to establish distinct geographic zones and issue localized special assessments.
